t:
(a) In General.—Section 25(f)(3) of the National Institute of Standards and Technology Act (15 U.S.C. 278k(f)(3)) is amended—
        (1) by striking “to develop” in the first sentence and inserting “to add capabilities to the MEP program, including the development of”; and 
        (2) by striking the last sentence and inserting “Centers may be reimbursed for costs incurred under the program. These themes—“(A) shall be related to projects designed to increase the viability both of traditional manufacturing sectors and other sectors, such as construction, that increasingly rely on manufacturing through the use of manufactured components and manufacturing techniques, including supply chain integration and quality management;“(B) shall be related to projects related to the transfer of technology based on the technological needs of manufacturers and available technologies from institutions of higher education, laboratories, and other technology producing entities; and“(C) may extend beyond these traditional areas to include projects related to construction industry modernization.”.  
    (b) Selection.—Section 25(f)(5) of the National Institute of Standards and Technology Act (15 U.S.C. 278k(f)(5)) is amended to read as follows:“(5) Selection.—“(A) In general.—Awards under this section shall be peer reviewed and competitively awarded. The Director shall endeavor to select at least one proposal in each of the 9 statistical divisions of the United States (as designated by the Bureau of the Census). The Director shall select proposals to receive awards that will—“(i) create jobs or train newly hired employees;“(ii) promote technology transfer and commercialization of environmentally focused materials, products, and processes;“(iii) increase energy efficiency; and“(iv) improve the competitiveness of industries in the region in which the Center or Centers are located.“(B) Additional selection criteria.—The Director may select proposals to receive awards that will—“(i) encourage greater cooperation and foster partnerships in the region with similar Federal, State, and locally funded programs to encourage energy efficiency and building technology; and“(ii) collect data and analyze the increasing connection between manufactured products and manufacturing techniques, the future of construction practices, and the emerging application of products from the green energy industries.”. 
    (c) Other Modifications.—Section 25(f) of the National Institute of Standards and Technology Act (15 U.S.C. 278k(f)) is amended—
        (1) by adding at the end the following:“(7) Duration.—Awards under this section shall last no longer than 3 years.“(8) Eligible participants.—In addition to manufacturing firms eligible to participate in the Centers program, awards under this subsection may be used by the Centers to assist small- or medium-sized construction firms. Centers may be reimbursed under the program for working with such eligible participants.“(9) Authorization of appropriations.—In addition to any amounts otherwise authorized or appropriated to carry out this section, there are authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary of Commerce $7,000,000 for each of the fiscal years 2011 through 2013 to carry out this subsection.”.

fable.w: The section amends a competitive grant program for MEP Centers, setting selection criteria, award duration, eligible firms and appropriations. The tempting reading treats "peer reviewed" and "eligible participants" as outside involvement, but the text does not say who the peer reviewers are or set up any consultation, comment, hearing or advisory process with non-federal parties. Applying for and receiving grant awards is expressly excluded from participation, and "participants" here only means firms served by the Centers.
fable.s: Awards under this section shall be peer reviewed and competitively awarded.

qwen_block.w: This section describes the process for selecting recipients of federal awards (grants). The definition explicitly states that participation 'does not include applications for benefits or grants.' The 'peer review' mentioned is part of the competitive selection process for these grants, not a mechanism for outside parties to consult with the government on policy decisions. The 'eligible participants' are applicants for funding, not participants in the decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: Awards under this section shall be peer reviewed and competitively awarded. The Director shall endeavor to select at least one proposal in each of the 9 statistical divisions of the United States
qwen_block.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "peer reviewed" implies participation by outside experts. However, peer review in the context of grant/award selection is typically an internal administrative procedure or a review by a panel that acts as part of the agency's decision-making apparatus, not necessarily a statutory requirement for public consultation or an advisory board with outside members. More importantly, the text describes the *selection criteria* for awards (grants), which the definition explicitly excludes ("It does not include applications for benefits or grants"). The "eligible participants" are those applying for the grants, not participants in the government's decision-making process. The section details how the Director selects proposals and who is eligible to receive money, which falls under the "applications for benefits or grants" exclusion.

opus.w: The only process language is peer review and competitive selection of grant proposals, which falls under the definition's exclusion for applications for grants, and the section does not say the reviewers are from outside the government. The State and local 'cooperation' language and the 'eligible participants' language describe selection criteria and who can get help, not federal consultation with outsiders before a decision. No hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue is created.
opus.s: Awards under this section shall be peer reviewed and competitively awarded.
opus.b:
**Step 1: The tempting reading and why it fails.** The tempting reading is "Yes," because "Awards under this section shall be peer reviewed" suggests outside experts may weigh in on a federal decision. Other phrases look like participation too: "encourage greater cooperation and foster partnerships... with similar Federal, State, and locally funded programs" and "Eligible participants."

On closer reading, each of these fails the definition:
- **Peer review:** It applies only to choosing which grant proposals to fund. The definition excludes applications for grants. The section also never says the reviewers come from outside the government.
- **"Encourage greater cooperation":** This is a criterion for judging proposals. It describes what the funded centers might do, not federal consultation with states before a decision.
- **"Eligible participants":** These are the construction firms that may receive help from the centers. They are beneficiaries, not participants in a federal decision.

No rulemaking, hearing, comment period, advisory committee or right to sue appears. The peer-review clause is a close call, so my confidence is moderate.

qwen_chat.w: The definition explicitly states that applications for benefits or grants are not participation. Peer review is a standard part of the grant application process, not a mechanism for outside parties to consult with the government on policy decisions. It looks like participation because it mentions "peer reviewed" awards and "eligible participants" who can receive grants.
qwen_chat.s: (A) In general.—Awards under this section shall be peer reviewed and competitively awarded.
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it mentions "peer reviewed" awards and "eligible participants" who can receive grants.
Resolution: The definition explicitly states that applications for benefits or grants are not participation. Peer review is a standard part of the grant application process, not a mechanism for outside parties to consult with the government on policy decisions.
